conventions.convention: Countable Choice is assumed throughout, including the Lebesgue, Hilbert, Fock and Fourier constructions.

Distributions are continuous complex-linear functionals on compact smooth tests with their fixed-support seminorms and locally convex inductive-limit topology; test pairing is bilinear. R^0 is a singleton of measure one.

The Hilbert pairing is second-variable-linear. Creation is linear and annihilation conjugate-linear in the one-particle vector. W(f,g) = ⟨Ω,J(conjugate(f))J(g)Ω⟩, tested against φ(f,g)(s) = ∫ conjugate(f(x+s))g(x) dx.
Positive type means nonnegativity of the tested covariance quadratic form, not positivity of J(f). The chiral one-particle sector is k > 0.

The symbol s−i0 denotes the lower boundary. The exponential coordinate Uκ(u) = −κ⁻¹exp(−κu) is increasing. The hyperbolic boundary is defined through the increasing diffeomorphism Yb(s) = sinh(bs)/b and is also identified with the analytic lower boundary.
The angular Fourier transform uses exp(−iωs), inverse factor 1/(2π), and bilinear transposition on tempered distributions. Detailed balance is S(−ω) = exp(βω)S(ω) for ω > 0.
For dimensionless b > 0, u′ = u/b, κ′ = bκ, ω′ = bω and β′ = β/b. Energy parameters use a fixed formal scale σ through ω = E/σ; no physical energy, clock or temperature identification is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice and Euclidean Lebesgue measure. For m ≥ 0, let dε: R^m × R → (0,∞) be smooth and real-valued, with positive lower and finite upper bounds and uniformly bounded first and second s-derivatives on every compact parameter set times bounded s-interval, for sufficiently small ε > 0. Then −(s−iεdε(v,s))⁻² converges on every compact smooth test to 1⊗B, where ⟨B,φ⟩ = ∫₀∞ k φ̂(k) dk and φ̂(k) = ∫ φ(s)exp(−iks) ds.

Assume Countable Choice. On H = L²((0,∞),dk;C), define hf(k) = sqrt(k/(4π))∫ f(U)exp(ikU)dU and J(f) = a(h_conjugate(f)) + a†(hf) on the invariant finite-particle domain. This is a complex-linear operator-valued distribution with vacuum covariance −1/[4π(s−i0)²]. For κ > 0, the compact-test coordinate construction jκ(g) = J(fg), with fg(U) = g(−κ⁻¹log(−κU)) for U < 0 and zero otherwise, has positive-type covariance Cκ(s) = −κ²/(16π)csch²(κ(s−i0)/2), with the explicitly defined test-coordinate boundary convention.

Assume Countable Choice. For A,b > 0, β = π/b and L = A/b², C(z) = −A csch²(bz) has a tempered lower boundary whose angular Fourier transform is the continuous nonnegative function S(ω) = 2πLω/(exp(βω)−1), with S(0) = 2A/b and S(−ω) = exp(βω)S(ω) for ω > 0. For A = κ²/(16π), b = κ/2, this is Cκ and Sκ(ω) = ω/[2(exp(2πω/κ)−1)], Sκ(0) = κ/(4π).

seams_checked.note: Checked the page prose and both consumer lemmas against the actual current and contour statements. The acceleration consumer uses α = a/c², u = cs and C_a(s) = π⁻¹C_α(cs), hence S_a(ν) = (πc)⁻¹S_α(ν/c). This preserves the lower boundary, normalization, zero-frequency value and detailed-balance exponent. The thermometer reproduces the chiral supplier formula faithfully and retains the accelerated chain's explicit conditional draft status. Neither consumer promotes the mathematical covariance result to a detector-probability theorem or empirical observation; the supplier page likewise excludes those interpretations.
